parsed.why: No criminalisation, no visitor-facing restriction; progressive constitutional rulings and incitement ban offset assembly-failure finding and documented public hostility. Worst features are societal friction and dated Pride obstruction, not state exposure.

Cross-dressing legal, gender change since 1982, EU-level protections, and convictions for assaults on trans tourists show working recourse. Residual transphobic violence and hostile rhetoric keep it below the top tier.

Decriminalised 2023, but no gender-identity protection, unregistrable LGBTI groups, election hate speech and a Pride cancelled by death threats: societal hostility with thin recourse, softened by PM support and welcoming tourism settings.

No criminalisation since 1890 and no documented visitor incidents, but governing doctrine brands transition 'threatening dignity', no protections exist, and LGBT people are excluded from diplomacy and employment — hostility without visitor-facing enforcement.

Morality offences reaching five years applied de facto to gender nonconformity and transition itself, plus documented militia torture and executions of gender-nonconforming people, religious bans on care, zero protections or recognition.
